title: Scalar-reduction adjunction unit and multiplication triangle
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with a final object [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $n\geq1$, and put $Z=\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C}$ and $R=(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)_{\mathcal C}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their cohomological unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $E=-\otimes_Z R$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], $Lq=-\otimes_Z^L R$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and let $\operatorname{Res}$ be restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. The sheaf coefficient sequence $0\to Z\xrightarrow{n}Z\to R\to0$ is exact [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. Every abelian sheaf killed by $n$ has a unique residue-module structure extending its integer action, and every additive map of such sheaves is $R$-linear [lem-pur-torsion-sheaf-constant-module]. Restriction $\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(Z)$ is fully faithful. There is a natural isomorphism $E(A)\simeq A/nA$, where $A/nA=\operatorname{coker}(n:A\to A)$ is a sheaf cokernel, sending $a\otimes\bar k$ to $ka\bmod nA$ and the ordinary adjunction unit to the quotient. For every ordinary adjunction $E'\dashv\operatorname{Res}$, its unit $A\to\operatorname{Res}E'(A)$ is likewise a cokernel of $n:A\to A$.
Let $A$ be an abelian sheaf and let $p:P\to A[0]$ be a flat-term K-flat resolution [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex]. The genuine $R$-complex $Q_A=E(P)=P/nP$ represents $Lq(A)$; let $c_A:Lq(A)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_A$ be its resolution comparison. The quotient $j:P\to\operatorname{Res}Q_A$ gives a degreewise short exact sequence $0\to P\xrightarrow{n}P\xrightarrow{j}\operatorname{Res}Q_A\to0$. With its canonical boundary $\partial_P:\operatorname{Res}Q_A\to P[1]$ [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle], transporting by $p,p,\operatorname{Res}(c_A)^{-1}$ gives a distinguished triangle
$$A\xrightarrow{n}A\xrightarrow{\eta_A}\operatorname{Res}Lq(A)\xrightarrow{\delta_A}A[1],\qquad\delta_A=p[1]\partial_P\operatorname{Res}(c_A).$$
Here $\eta$ is the normalized derived unit whose value on a K-flat complex is the ordinary termwise unit [lem-sfb-scalar-adjunction-unit-coefficient-normalization]. Multiplication by $n$ is monic in every term of any flat-term complex, whether or not its cohomology is concentrated in degree zero. The residue kernel and quotient structures therefore give the corresponding data of [def-sfb-scalar-reduction-presentation] for every extension satisfying its monic and epic multiplication hypotheses.

proof.text: The constant presheaf sequence $0\to\mathbf Z\xrightarrow{n}\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z\to0$ is sectionwise exact: $n\geq1$ makes multiplication injective and the residue map has kernel $n\mathbf Z$. Sheafification is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact]. Applying it to this sequence gives $0\to Z\xrightarrow{n}Z\to R\to0$, since these constant sheaves are precisely the sheafifications of the constant presheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. This is also exact in $Z$-modules, whose kernels and cokernels have the underlying abelian-sheaf kernels and cokernels [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Tag 093J (lemma-constant-exact), proof by exact sheafification; Tag 03CN (lemma-abelian-abelian).

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-torsion-sheaf-constant-module] with $N=n$: every sheaf killed by $n$ has the unique stated residue action and every additive map between two such sheaves is residue-linear. Every $R$-module is killed by $n$ because $n\bar1=0$. Thus restriction is full, since an integral-linear map between restricted residue modules is additive and hence residue-linear. It is faithful because restriction leaves the underlying maps unchanged [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars].

source.place: Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), applied to the residue actions as in the cited torsion-module lemma.

proof.text: Let $\pi:A\to T=\operatorname{coker}(n:A\to A)$. Since $(n_T)\pi=\pi n_A=0$ and $\pi$ is epic, $n_T=0$; give $T$ its unique residue action by [lem-pur-torsion-sheaf-constant-module]. Write $u_A:A\to\operatorname{Res}E(A)$ for the ordinary unit, $a\mapsto a\otimes\bar1$, using the ordinary adjunction formulas of [lem-sfb-scalar-adjunction-unit-coefficient-normalization]. Balancing gives $u_A(na)=a\otimes n\bar1=0$. The cokernel property gives $v:T\to\operatorname{Res}E(A)$ with $v\pi=u_A$; this map is residue-linear by the torsion-module lemma. The adjunct of $\pi$ is $f:E(A)\to T$ with $(\operatorname{Res}f)u_A=\pi$. Hence $fv\pi=\pi$, so $fv=1_T$; also $(vf)u_A=u_A$, so injectivity of the adjunction bijection gives $vf=1_{E(A)}$. These are inverse isomorphisms. The adjunction formula gives $f(a\otimes\bar k)=k\pi(a)$; local representatives suffice for arbitrary sections of the constant residue sheaf. The equality $fu_A=\pi$ identifies the unit, and uniqueness of cokernel factorizations proves naturality in $A$. Thus $E(A)\simeq A/nA$ is the asserted natural isomorphism, in the residue-module category, with the specified quotient unit.

source.place: Tag 03D7 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules), specialized to the identity topos and Z to R; the displayed inverse Hom formulas and the cokernel universal property.

proof.text: For any other ordinary adjunction $E'\dashv\operatorname{Res}$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] with $L_1=E$, $L_2=E'$ and both right adjoints equal to restriction. It gives an isomorphism $c:E\simeq E'$ satisfying $(\operatorname{Res}c_A)u_A=u'_A$. Step 3 says that $u_A$ is a cokernel of $n_A$. Postcomposing a cokernel with an isomorphism is a cokernel: a map killing $n_A$ factors uniquely through $u_A$ and then through $(\operatorname{Res}c_A)^{-1}$. This proves the assertion for the actual unit of every such adjunction.

Let $M$ be any flat $Z$-module sheaf. By [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], the functor $-\otimes_Z M$ is exact; apply it to the coefficient sequence proved in step 1. The resulting sequence is $0\to M\xrightarrow{n}M\to R\otimes_Z M\to0$: the identification $Z\otimes_Z M\simeq M$ is $z\otimes m\mapsto zm$ with inverse $m\mapsto1\otimes m$. Switching the two factors is $r\otimes m\mapsto m\otimes r$, inverse to the same switch; these balanced maps induce maps of sheafifications by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The last map is consequently $m\mapsto m\otimes\bar1$, identified with the quotient in step 3. Thus $n:M\to M$ is monic. Apply this argument independently to every term of any flat-term complex: it uses no hypothesis on its cohomology or boundedness.

source.place: Tag 03ER (definition-flat), item (3); explicit tensor unit and switch maps.

proof.text: For the given resolution $p:P\to A[0]$, apply [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] with $\mathcal O=Z$, $\mathcal O'=R$. Its K-flat computation gives the comparison $c_A:Lq(A)\simeq E(P)$. The natural quotient identification in step 3 applied termwise identifies this genuine $R$-complex with $Q_A=P/nP$; naturality makes its quotient maps commute with the differentials. Step 5 applied in every degree now gives the degreewise short exact sequence $0\to P\xrightarrow{n}P\xrightarrow{j}\operatorname{Res}Q_A\to0$. In particular the residue action is on an actual complex, not merely on its cohomology.

source.place: Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), with the K-flat construction before Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] to the short exact sequence of complexes from step 6 in the abelian category of $Z$-module sheaves. It gives the distinguished triangle $P\xrightarrow{n}P\xrightarrow{j}\operatorname{Res}Q_A\xrightarrow{\partial_P}P[1]$. Use its canonical short-exact-sequence boundary, with the sign fixed by the cited delta-functor construction (Stacks Tag 0152), throughout.

source.place: Tag 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor), with boundary -p composed with the inverse cone-to-quotient comparison.

proof.text: Write $p$ also for its image in the derived category; it is invertible by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $c_P:Lq(P)\simeq E(P)$ be the K-flat comparison. The resolution comparisons in [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] satisfy $c_A Lq(p)=c_P$: $c_A$ is the comparison obtained by inverting the map induced by this resolution. The normalized unit formula of [lem-sfb-scalar-adjunction-unit-coefficient-normalization] is $(\operatorname{Res}c_P)\eta_P=j$. Naturality gives $\eta_Ap=\operatorname{Res}(Lq(p))\eta_P$, hence $(\operatorname{Res}c_A)\eta_Ap=j$. Transport the triangle of step 7 by the isomorphisms $(p,p,(\operatorname{Res}c_A)^{-1})$. Its second arrow is $(\operatorname{Res}c_A)^{-1}jp^{-1}=\eta_A$ and its last arrow is $p[1]\partial_P\operatorname{Res}(c_A)$. Its first arrow remains $n$, because $pn=np$. These equations verify each square of the triangle isomorphism, including the shifted final square. Distinguished triangles are closed under isomorphism by [def-weil-triangulated-category]. This proves exactly the triangle and boundary formula in the statement.

source.place: K-flat derived pullback construction, Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), combined with Tag 0152 (derived.tex) and the stated unit normalization.

proof.text: Finally let $0\to B\to M\to F\to0$ be any extension with $n:B\to B$ epic and $n:F\to F$ monic. Put $H=\ker(n:B\to B)$ and $T=\operatorname{coker}(n:F\to F)$. Multiplication by $n$ kills $H$ by its kernel inclusion and kills $T$ by its epic quotient, so [lem-pur-torsion-sheaf-constant-module] supplies their unique residue structures. The sequences $0\to\operatorname{Res}H\to B\xrightarrow{n}B\to0$ and $0\to F\xrightarrow{n}F\to\operatorname{Res}T\to0$ are short exact: their middle exactness is the kernel/cokernel property, and the endpoint conditions are precisely the assumed epimorphy and monicity [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. The composites with multiplication vanish by those same properties. Taking these maps and residue objects together with the given extension supplies every datum of [def-sfb-scalar-reduction-presentation].
